title: Olympic Beach Volleyball: Road to Gold
text:
Atlanta 1996 — Paris 2024



Follow beach volleyball from its Olympic debut to a new generation of champions. This story uses athlete-event records to put the sport in the wider Olympic picture—and team results to trace every medal.

Explore the data →

title: Olympic Beach Volleyball: Road to Gold
section: One point per Olympic volleyball athlete-event
text:
One point per Olympic volleyball athlete-event
Age at each Games, 1964–2024. The indoor records provide a longer Olympic history for context: indoor volleyball debuted in 1964, while beach volleyball joined in 1996. Hover for athlete, team, sex, and medal details. Slight jitter separates overlapping age-and-year values; it changes display position only.


4,783 real athlete-event observations plotted


756 beach volleyball observations


4,027 indoor volleyball observations






Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes. Each point is one age-reported Summer Olympic Volleyball athlete-event record (4,783 of 4,792); gold highlights all 756 beach volleyball records from 1996–2024.








NoteWhat the data can—and cannot—show



The source documentation defines each row as one athlete’s participation in a Games and event; the records have athlete IDs and do not include coaches or other staff. This chart includes Summer Volleyball records with reported age. Of 4,792 such event records from 1964–2024, 756 are beach volleyball across eight Games (84 in 1996 and 96 per edition from 2000 through 2024), and 4,027 are indoor volleyball. Nine Volleyball records have no age and are not plotted.
The beach-only subset is too small to supply thousands of distinct observations. Indoor volleyball is included as historical context for the longer Olympic timeline, while its smaller, muted markers keep beach volleyball prominent. The chart shows every age-reported Volleyball record once; a beach-specific graphic with thousands of points would need an additional rally-by-rally dataset, such as official FIVB/Volleyball World DataVolley records for Olympic beach matches.


Continue to Olympic Trends to compare participation across Summer Games.
Sources: olympicAthletes package and data documentation. See methodology and results sources for team-medal counting and the recent podium supplement.

title: Olympic Trends
text:
One Olympic timeline, three lenses
The broadest view follows every Summer Olympic athlete-event entry. The gold trace then zooms in: first on all indoor and beach Volleyball entries, then on beach volleyball alone, identified from the event field. Each panel has its own vertical scale so the specialist event remains visible.





Athlete-event entries at Summer Olympic Games. Panels use separate vertical scales.




Because each panel has its own vertical scale, compare the shape of the trends rather than their heights across panels. Beach volleyball entries first appear in 1996 (84 athlete-event rows) and reach 96 in 2000, where they remain through 2024.

title: Olympic Trends
text:
Athlete ages across the Games
These points show individual beach-volleyball athlete-event records, not yearly averages. The spread reveals the age range within each event and how it changes across editions.




Each point is one of 756 beach-volleyball athlete-event records from 1996–2024. Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes.



Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes; 756 athlete-event rows from 1996–2024. Age is present for every beach-volleyball record in this source.

Because each marker is a real athlete-event record, repeated appearances by the same athlete in different editions remain separate rows and are not synthetic extra observations.






NoteWhat counts as a record?



One row represents one athlete at one Games edition in one event—not one unique person or one team. Beach volleyball is filtered from event within the Volleyball sport, rather than treating all Volleyball entries as beach volleyball.


The Men vs. Women page focuses on beach volleyball participation and podiums by event.

title: Men vs Women
text:
Beach volleyball has featured men’s and women’s tournaments at every Games since its 1996 debut. Participation is measured in athlete-event records—two records for each competing pair—while podium results count each country-team once.


Each point is a beach-volleyball athlete-event record. The age-height relationship is compared by event; shapes show medals only where the source records them.




Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes. Shows r scales::comma(nrow(athlete_profiles)) of r scales::comma(nrow(beach_athletes)) athlete-event records with reported height; medal status is unavailable in the source for 2020 and 2024.



Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes. The chart plots 668 of 756 athlete-event records with reported height; records without height are omitted. Medal status is not reported by this source for 2020 or 2024.









Beach volleyball participation by event and Games year. Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes; 756 athlete-event records across eight editions.




Recorded participation begins lower for women at the sport’s debut: 36 athlete-event rows versus 48 for men in 1996. From 2000 through 2024, both events have 48 rows per Games in this dataset; these are athlete-event counts, not audience or popularity measures.







Each point is one of 48 medal-winning country-teams. Panels compare men’s and women’s results by Olympic year; 2020 and 2024 podiums use official Olympic results.



Sources: olympicAthletes for 1996–2016; official Olympic results for Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. The plot shows all 48 country-team medal results once each, not once per athlete.

Across eight editions, each event awards 24 team medals. Brazil leads both tallies (8 women’s and 6 men’s medals), while the United States has 7 women’s and 4 men’s; Australia’s three medals are all in the women’s event.

title: About
text:
About the project
This site explores the history, global participation, competitive performance, and evolution of Olympic beach volleyball through data analysis. It follows the sport from its Olympic debut in Atlanta in 1996 to the Paris 2024 Games.


GitHub profile
Project repository
New College of Florida

title: About
text:
Data and methods

Dataset and sources
The primary source is olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes, a dataset of 315,094 Olympic athlete-event records. Filtering to Summer Games Volleyball events identified as beach volleyball gives 756 beach-volleyball athlete-event records, covering eight editions: 1996, 2000, 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024.
The package documents historical sources including the Olympic history dataset and Olympedia. For recent podiums, I use the official Tokyo 2020 results and official Paris 2024 results.


Methodology
I use R to load and prepare the data: filter to Summer Games, Volleyball, and beach-volleyball events; count participation as athlete-event rows; and standardize country labels from team identifiers for country-level comparisons. For medal analysis, I count each country-team’s result once per Games, event, and medal rather than counting both athletes on a pair as separate medals. Because medal labels are unavailable in the package for 2020 and 2024, I add those podiums from the official results above.
I build the visualizations with ggplot2, Plotly, and Leaflet, and use Quarto to render the interactive website.

title: About
text:
Data limitations
An athlete-event row is not a unique person: athletes who compete in multiple Games appear in multiple rows. The source also has incomplete country/team identifiers for recent editions: 171 of its 192 beach-volleyball records from 2020 and 2024 lack a country derived from the team field. For that reason, the country participation map is limited to 1996–2016 rather than assigning countries to records with missing identifiers. The 2020 and 2024 podiums are included only where official results support team-medal counts. Some athlete characteristics, including height, are also missing for a portion of records.

A medal race across eight editions
Each line tracks a country’s cumulative team medals from Atlanta to Paris. Use the filters to focus on a country or event; hover over a point for the edition-by-edition total. Every podium finish counts once for its pair and event.






Country

Cumulative beach volleyball team medals by country and event, 1996–2024. Source: olympicAthletes through 2016 and official Olympic results for 2020 and 2024.



Sources: olympicAthletes through 2016 and official Olympic results for Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. The 48 medal-team results are converted to 240 cumulative country/event/year values; zero-medal years are shown as zero, not as extra medal results.

Each rise reflects one or more medal-winning country-teams; a pair earns one team medal rather than two athlete medals. Brazil and the United States finish highest at 14 and 11 team medals, while the country and event filters let you compare how those totals accumulated.

What those medals are made of
The next chart compares gold, silver, and bronze team medals by country. Hover for exact counts. Country totals include both men’s and women’s events across 1996–2024.




Gold, silver, and bronze team medals by country, 1996–2024. Source: olympicAthletes through 2016 and official Olympic results for 2020 and 2024.



Sources: olympicAthletes through 2016 and official Olympic results for Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. Medal-type totals combine the 48 distinct country-team podium results.

Brazil’s seven silvers equal the United States’ seven golds, even though Brazil leads in total medals. Hover each stack to compare a country’s medal mix; use the map filters above for the edition-specific view.
Data note: the 2020 and 2024 athlete-event records do not carry beach-volleyball medal labels in this release of the source. Their podium teams are added from the Tokyo 2020 results and Paris 2024 results, not inferred from missing values.

title: Road to Gold
text:
Since beach volleyball joined the Olympic programme in 1996, Brazil has earned 14 team medals, including 4 golds. Brazil reached the podium at every Games from 1996 through 2016, then returned to the top of the women’s podium in Paris. The United States is next with 11 medals, 7 of them gold, built across both men’s and women’s events.
Success has never belonged to just two flags. Australia won women’s gold in 2000; Germany’s golds came in the men’s event in 2012 and the women’s in 2016; and China took silver and bronze in the 2008 women’s competition. More recently, Norway and Sweden captured men’s gold in Tokyo and Paris, while Qatar earned men’s bronze at both editions.

Every medal, counted once
The chart counts a medal for the country-team pair in an event, not for each athlete on that pair. Each edition awards three medals in each of two events, giving 48 team medals across eight editions.




Country totals aggregate 48 beach-volleyball team medals across eight editions. Sources: olympicAthletes through 2016 and official Olympic results for 2020 and 2024.



Sources: olympicAthletes through 2016 and official Olympic results for Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. Country and medal-type totals aggregate 48 team-medal results.

Brazil leads the total with 14 team medals, while the United States has 11. Their medal mixes differ: Brazil’s seven silvers match the U.S. seven golds, so the overall leader is not the gold-medal leader.

title: Road to Gold
text:
Methodology

The source is olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes, a 315,094-row, 16-column athlete-event dataset. The package describes 1896–2016 records as extending the Olympic history dataset, with later records sourced from Olympedia.
Beach volleyball is selected by requiring sport == "Volleyball" and a beach-volleyball match in event. The package’s 4,792-row volleyball_athletes subset contains indoor and beach volleyball; it is not used as a beach-volleyball count.
For 1996–2016, the source repeats the medal on both athletes’ rows. We retain one row for each Games year, event, team identifier, and medal, then normalize team suffixes (such as -1) only when aggregating results by country.
The package data used here has no beach-volleyball medal labels for 2020 or 2024. We add the six podium teams for each of those editions from the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 official results pages. These are team-level rows, so no athlete-level medal duplication is introduced.
Participation charts count athlete-event rows; medal charts count medal-winning teams. A pair therefore contributes two participation records but only one medal.
To render the site, install R packages olympicAthletes, tidyverse, ggplot2, plotly, crosstalk, leaflet, rnaturalearth, and geojsonsf, then run quarto render.

For other country results, edition details, and filters, head to Country Explorer.
